character_sheet: A hostile armoured trooper bug: a ten-plate head with two eyes on bases, two antennae, two ridges, an upper jaw of nine plates with two ridges and six teeth, a lower jaw of twelve plates with a tongue, four mouth edges and an inner mouth, two mandible arms of six plates and two palps of four, and four legs of a coxa, a shoulder, a two-plate femur with an elbow, a three-plate tibia and a four-plate tarsus, all on a two-piece hip hub (TrooperBugModel.java:294-966, 134 parts), drawn at x1.1. 200 HP, 20 damage, 15 armour, speed 0.4 (MobStats.java:106; EntityTrooperBug.java:99-106). On a 1-in-5 tick it picks prey in a 12-block box - anything but the hydrolisc, the ender reaper and knight, endermen, creepers, its own kind, spit bugs and creative players (:237-238, :269-282, :307-337) - and one time in thirty conjures a Spit Bug between itself and its target (:240-251); it chases at 1.2 and, within 5 blocks plus half the target's width, rolls its bite on a 1-in-5 cadence for 20 with a 1.8 knockback (:88, :172-189; BugMeleeAttackGoal.Params.trooperBug; BugMeleeAttackGoal.java:159-174); between 4 and 8 blocks, on the ground, one cadence tick in ten it LEAPS - a 1.15 upward, 0.2-0.65 forward jump with its navigation cut (TrooperBugLeapAttackGoal.java:29-42; :147-170); the synched DATA_ATTACKING int (:46-47) is held at 1 in reach and on the leap. It takes one hit per 20 ticks and ignores falls and cactus (:191-216). It spawns in the dark, by day only on a 2-in-20 roll, with clear air about it (:344-351; ModEntities.java:307-309). Read it as a paratrooper beetle: a slow heavy four-leg scuttle, every mouthpart twitching at rest and thrashing when it fights, the leap its signature.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.1 of the rig (TrooperBugRenderer.java:24, :36; shadow 1.045, :26) on a 512x256 sheet (TrooperBugModel.java:968), trooperbug.png (TrooperBugRenderer.java:20); the hitbox is 3.0 x 3.5 (ModEntities.java:307-309). The original's ModelTrooperBug(0.22f) argument was the wingspeed (TrooperBugModel.java:21), not a scale. Each leg is a position chain the code re-places each tick (26 px to the tibia, 32 to the tarsus; :1169-1311) - key the joints, not the positions.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: sweep: pi x 0.12 = 0.377 rad (22 deg) x the walking speed as a sine, every moving piece of a leg yawing together about the femur's rest (1.2 for the right front); lift: |cos| x pi x 0.12 x the speed on the rising half of the sine only, added to the femur plates' pitches (1.115 / 1.078) and the tarsus plates' (1.08) and subtracted from the tibia plates' (1.871 / 1.817 / 1.762); the left front takes the sine, the left rear its negative, the right pair the same half a cycle later; the tibia is placed 26 px along the femur and the tarsus 32 along the tibia; the coxae and shoulders are static; no threshold
groups.plain: the four legs sweep about the vertical in two opposed pairs and each leg bends at the knee as it swings forward, the whole leg placed link by link - slow and heavy
groups.math: s = sin(t * 2.0 * 0.22) * pi * 0.12 * amount; up = (sin at t + 0.1 > s) ? |cos(t * 2.0 * 0.22) * pi * 0.12 * amount| : 0; leftFront(s, up); leftRear(-s, up); s' = sin(t * 2.0 * 0.22 + pi) * pi * 0.12 * amount (up' likewise); rightFront(-s', up'); rightRear(s', up'); per leg: femur, elbow, tibia and tarsus pieces yRot = rest + angle; femur xRot = 1.115 / 1.078 + up; tibia xRot = 1.871 / 1.817 / 1.762 - up; tarsus xRot = 1.08 + up; positions chained by cos / sin of the yaw x 26 and 32
groups.source: TrooperBugModel.java:1013-1028 (the phases), :1169-1311 (the four leg helpers); wingspeed 0.22 (:21)
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 2.0 x 0.22 = 0.44: the natural period is 14.3 ticks

groups.plain: the two mandible claws pitch against each other: a slow small working at rest, a wide fast chomp while the attacking flag is up
groups.math: m = attacking ? cos(t * 2.6 * 0.22) * pi * 0.2 : cos(t * 0.3 * 0.22) * pi * 0.05; arm1part3.xRot = arm1part3b.xRot = 1.56 + m; arm2part3.xRot = arm2part3b.xRot = 1.56 - m

behaviour: One gait rhythm with no threshold (TrooperBugModel.java:1013-1028): a sine at 0.44 rad/tick (a 14-tick period) sweeps each leg's ten moving pieces 22 degrees x the walking speed about the femur's splay, the left front and left rear in opposition and the right pair the same half a cycle later; on the rising half a |cos| lift of the same size bends the femur and tarsus up and the tibia down - the step. Every leg is placed link by link along its yaw (26 and 32 px; :1169-1311); the coxae and shoulders never move.

Five branches on the synched DATA_ATTACKING int (EntityTrooperBug.java:46-47), held at 1 while it stands within 5 blocks plus half the target's width (BugMeleeAttackGoal.java:168) and on a leap (TrooperBugLeapAttackGoal.java:38), dropped otherwise (:132, :145, :176): at rest the antennae, palps, mandibles, ridges and jaw all creep on slow cosines (9, 9, 9, 3.6 and 2.7 degrees at 0.088, 0.11, 0.066, 0.022 and 0.066 rad/tick); attacking they thrash (18, 27, 36, 18 and 18 degrees at 0.308, 0.55, 0.572, 0.22 and 0.572 rad/tick) (:978-1012).

The hip hub, the head plates and root, the eyes, the antenna bases, the upper jaw plates and tips, the six teeth, the inner mouth, the mouth edges, the tongue, the mandible arms' upper and middle plates and the palp roots are static; there is no head bone and no look. The bite (doHurtTarget, EntityTrooperBug.java:172-189), the leap (jumpFromGround :147-162 from TrooperBugLeapAttackGoal.java:29-42) and the Spit Bug summon (:240-251) are not animation events.
